capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia lists the 77.4 kWh pack for the first generation; the GT uses the same E-GMP long-range pack. GT-specific 2023-2024 page not opened.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database usable 74.0 kWh for the 77.4 kWh first-generation EV6 pack; the GT (2022-2024) uses the same pack.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Same 77.4 kWh pack as the Long Range EV6 (NMC per EV Database).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: E-GMP 800 V (697 V) pack shared with the Long Range EV6.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: 2024 EV6 manual (via ManualsLib) shows a Battery conditioning mode setting in EV Settings plus the DC-charger-as-destination trigger; Kia says the feature is standard from MY23 and was a retrofit for MY22 (src-insideevs-ev6-cold-weather-update, Europe). Compared model years 2022-2024; same first-generation hardware. The manual says it needs a battery heater; not confirmed per Canadian/US trim.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia gives 240 kW for the 77.4 kWh pack; the GT uses the same pack and DC hardware (Kia quotes the same 18 min 10-80 %).

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs relaying Kia US specs gives 10.9 kW for the 2022 58 and 77.4 kWh EV6 packs; the GT uses the same 77.4 kWh pack and charger (no GT-specific page).
